title: "Show me the market"
hook: offered half his brother's wealth, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf asks only to be shown the market (Bukhari)

segments.voice: Yesterday, the people of the bench, poor companions living in the mosque. Your line was: the bench of the poor. Which learner came to mind, and what could you give them? Day seven hundred seventy-three.

Two strangers, made brothers. When the emigrants arrived in Medina with almost nothing, the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, paired them up with the people of the city. Newcomers were given local brothers. Bukhari keeps one of those pairings in the newcomer's own words. Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, from Mecca, is paired with Sa'd ibn al-Rabi', from Medina. And Sa'd, almost at once, makes him an enormous offer. Today: show me the market.
screen: `STRANGERS MADE BROTHERS.` → `ABD AL-RAHMAN AND SA'D.` → `AN OFFER ON THE TABLE.`

segments.voice: Sa'd says, in Abd al-Rahman's telling: I am the wealthiest of the Ansar. I will divide my wealth in half, and half is yours. Weigh that offer. This is not a meal or a loan. It is half of everything, given to a man he has just met, because the Prophet called them brothers. Abd al-Rahman's answer is the line we're carrying today. He says, in effect: I have no need of that. Is there a market here where trade goes on? Sa'd tells him: the market of Qaynuqa. The next morning Abd al-Rahman is there. He buys and sells dried curd and clarified butter, small goods, and keeps going back day after day. Before long, Bukhari says, he turns up with a trace of yellow perfume on him, the sign of a bridegroom. He has earned enough to marry. Look at the two men side by side. Neither of them is the hero alone. Sa'd's generosity is real and total: he offered half, and meant it. Abd al-Rahman's refusal is not pride. He answers with thanks, and with a blessing on Sa'd's family and wealth. What he asks for instead is a door: not the money, but the place where money is honestly made. Both are kindness. One gives. The other protects the giver, and keeps his own dignity. The brotherhood stayed whole, and so did both men's dignity.
screen: `HALF OF EVERYTHING IS YOURS.` · `IS THERE A MARKET HERE?` · `CURD AND BUTTER, DAY AFTER DAY.` · `ONE GIVES, ONE PROTECTS THE GIVER.` · then, large: `SHOW ME THE MARKET.`

segments.voice: The practice: earn something honestly. Sit, and let your breathing slow. Think about your work, paid or unpaid, and the way you earn what you have. Notice one place where it's honest and clean, and let yourself be glad of it. Then notice one place that could be cleaner: a shortcut, an exaggeration, a corner cut. Don't argue with it. Just see it. Choose one small thing you'll do today to earn your keep straight. If you pray, you can ask Allah to bless what you earn. Rest there. The bell holds the time.
Show me the market. Offered half his new brother's wealth, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf thanks him, refuses, and asks only for the way to the market. Today's word.
Your line: show me the market. Today, when someone offers to carry you, thank them, and ask for the door instead. Day seven hundred seventy-three.

howItsDone: Muslims tell the story of Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf and Sa'd ibn al-Rabi' when speaking of the brotherhood (mu'akhah) between the emigrants and the Ansar, and of earning an honest living.

I'll take a loan, not a gift.
fork.reveal: Abd al-Rahman blessed Sa'd's family and wealth, refused, and asked for the market. by the next morning he was trading.

original.note: Arabic: 'the market'; Abd al-Rahman asks to be shown the market.

trapdoor: what you thought: a man too proud to take help.
what it means: one brother gives everything, the other protects him by earning his own way, and both are kindness.
what a scholar hears: Bukhari 2048 and 2049, Abd al-Rahman's own report; the brotherhood (mu'akhah) and the market of Banu Qaynuqa.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 2048 (Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf: brotherhood with Sa'd ibn al-Rabi'; offer of half his wealth; the market of Qaynuqa; dried curd and butter; the trace of saffron)

notes: Bukhari 2048 and 2049 numbers cited from memory; confirm.
In the hadith Sa'd also offers to divorce one of his two wives so that Abd al-Rahman could marry her; left out of the script for this audience. Confirm the omission is acceptable.
'I am the wealthiest of the Ansar' is Sa'd's own claim in the hadith, reported as his words; confirm.
Abd al-Rahman's blessing on Sa'd's family and wealth is in Bukhari 2049 (Anas); confirm.
'Paired them up with the people of the city': the mu'akhah; script gives no count of pairs.

Audit pass: 'each newcomer was given a local brother' (a count no cited text gives) became 'newcomers were given local brothers'; 'saffron' became 'yellow perfume' (sufrah; confirm the wording); cut 'nobody had to carry anybody', which cast Sa'd's offer as a burden.

Editor pass: cut the flourish 'by a single word' from the hook (no cited text says how the pairing was made); 'Think about what that offer means' became 'Weigh that offer' to avoid the banned 'Think' opener pattern.
